docs.title: Chess Board Drawer Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the Chess Board Drawer documentation! This application allows you to create and customize chess boards using Python's Turtle graphics library.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Chess Board Drawer is a Python application that:

  • Visualizes chess boards with customizable sizes (4×4 to 16×16)
  • Offers multiple color themes
  • Includes animation toggle
  • Features a clean UI with intuitive controls
  • Connects to a chess game module

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Interactive Board Customization: Change board size and color theme in real time
  • Multiple Color Themes: Classic, Vintage, Purple, Gray, Blue, Red
  • Animation Control: Toggle animation effects on or off
  • Chess Game Integration: Launch a full chess game with your selected theme

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Run the chess board drawer
python turtle_chessboard.py

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.6+
  • Turtle graphics module (included in standard Python installation)
  • Tkinter (for the chess game component)

docs.title: Chess Board Drawer
docs.text:
A visual chess board creator and customizer built with Python's Turtle graphics.

This module provides an interactive application for generating chess boards with customizable sizes, color themes, and animation options. It features a clean user interface with buttons for theme selection, board size adjustment, and animation toggling.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Multiple color themes (Classic, Vintage, Purple, Gray, Blue, Red)
  • Adjustable board sizes (4×4 to 16×16)
  • Animation on/off toggle
  • Integration with a chess game module

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Run the chess board drawer application
python turtle_chessboard.py

docs.title: Dependencies

  • Turtle graphics (included in standard Python installation)
  • Tkinter (for chess game integration)

def change_board_size(delta):
    """
    Change the board size by the specified delta.

    Args:
        delta (int): Amount to change the board size by (+1 to increase, -1 to decrease)

    Returns:
        None

    Note:
        The board size is constrained to be between 4 and 16 inclusive.
        The square size is automatically adjusted to fit the screen.
    """
    global current_size

    # Update size with constraints
    new_size = current_size + delta
    if 4 <= new_size <= 16:
        current_size = new_size

        # Calculate appropriate square size based on screen
        square_size = min(600 // current_size, 70)

        # Redraw the board
        draw_board(current_size, square_size, current_theme)

        # Redraw UI elements
        draw_ui_elements()

def change_theme(theme_name):
    """
    Change the color theme and redraw the board.

    Args:
        theme_name (str): Name of the theme to apply (must be a key in color_themes)

    Returns:
        None

    Raises:
        KeyError: If the theme_name is not found in color_themes

    Example:
        ```python
        change_theme("Blue")  # Changes to the blue theme
        ```
    """
    global current_theme
    current_theme = theme_name

    # Calculate appropriate square size based on screen and board size
    square_size = min(600 // current_size, 70)

    # Redraw the board with new theme
    draw_board(current_size, square_size, current_theme)

    # Redraw UI elements
    draw_ui_elements()

def check_animation_button_click(x, y):
    """
    Check if the animation toggle button was clicked.

    Args:
        x (float): X-coordinate of the click
        y (float): Y-coordinate of the click

    Returns:
        bool: True if the animation button was clicked, False otherwise

    Note:

    """
    size_y = -308

    if 210 <= x <= 270 and size_y <= y <= size_y + 25:
        toggle_animation()
        return True

    return False

def check_size_button_click(x, y):
    """
    Check if a size control button was clicked and respond accordingly.

    Args:
        x (float): X-coordinate of the click
        y (float): Y-coordinate of the click

    Returns:
        bool: True if a size control button was clicked, False otherwise

    Note:

        corresponding button is clicked.
    """
    size_y = -308

    # Check decrease button
    if -170 <= x <= -130 and size_y <= y <= size_y + 25:
        change_board_size(-1)
        return True

    # Check increase button
    if -70 <= x <= -30 and size_y <= y <= size_y + 25:
        change_board_size(1)
        return True

    return False

def check_theme_button_click(x, y):
    """
    Check if a theme button was clicked and respond accordingly.

    Args:
        x (float): X-coordinate of the click
        y (float): Y-coordinate of the click

    Returns:
        bool: True if a theme button was clicked, False otherwise

    Note:
        This function will change the current theme if a theme button is clicked.
    """
    theme_y = -250
    button_width = 70
    button_height = 30
    x_pos = -200

    for theme in color_themes:
        # Check if click is within this button
        if x_pos <= x <= x_pos + button_width and theme_y <= y <= theme_y + button_height:
            change_theme(theme)
            return True

        x_pos += button_width + 10

    return False

Parameters:

def draw_board(size=8, square_size=50, theme_name="Classic"):
    """
    Draw a complete chess board with the given parameters.

    This function creates a chess board centered on the screen with the specified
    size, square dimensions, and color theme. For standard 8×8 boards, it also
    adds row and column labels (a-h, 1-8).

    Args:
        size (int): Number of squares per side (default: 8)
        square_size (int): Size of each square in pixels (default: 50)
        theme_name (str): Name of the color theme to use (default: "Classic")

    Returns:
        None

    Note:
        The board is drawn centered on the screen, with the origin (0,0) at the center.
        Row and column labels are only added for standard 8×8 boards.
    """
    # Get colors from the theme
    light_color = color_themes[theme_name]["light"]
    dark_color = color_themes[theme_name]["dark"]

    # Calculate the total board size
    board_size = size * square_size

    # Calculate starting position to center the board
    start_x = -board_size / 2
    start_y = -board_size / 2 + 100  # Moved up to reduce top padding

    # Clear previous drawings
    board_drawer.clear()

    # Draw all squares
    for row in range(size):
        for col in range(size):
            # Determine square color (alternating pattern)
            color = light_color if (row + col) % 2 == 0 else dark_color

            # Calculate position for this square
            x = start_x + col * square_size
            y = start_y + row * square_size

            # Draw the square
            draw_square(board_drawer, x, y, square_size, color)

    # Draw border around the board
    board_drawer.penup()
    board_drawer.goto(start_x, start_y)
    board_drawer.pendown()
    board_drawer.pensize(1)  # Reduced border size
    board_drawer.color("black")
    for _ in range(4):
        board_drawer.forward(board_size)
        board_drawer.left(90)

    # Draw labels (a-h, 1-8) for a standard 8x8 board
    if size == 8:
        # Draw column labels (a-h)
        board_drawer.penup()
        for col in range(8):
            x = start_x + col * square_size + square_size / 2
            y = start_y - 25
            board_drawer.goto(x, y)
            board_drawer.write(chr(97 + col), align="center", font=("Arial", 12, "normal"))

        # Draw row labels (1-8)
        for row in range(8):
            x = start_x - 25
            y = start_y + row * square_size + square_size / 2 - 6
            board_drawer.goto(x, y)
            board_drawer.write(str(row + 1), align="center", font=("Arial", 12, "normal"))

    screen.update()  # Update the screen after drawing

def draw_button(t, x, y, width, height, fill_color, text, text_color="black"):
    """
    Draw an interactive button with text.

    Args:
        t (turtle.Turtle): The turtle object to use for drawing
        x (float): X-coordinate of the bottom-left corner
        y (float): Y-coordinate of the bottom-left corner
        width (float): Width of the button in pixels
        height (float): Height of the button in pixels
        fill_color (str): Color name or hex code for the button background
        text (str): Text to display on the button
        text_color (str, optional): Color for the button text (default: "black")

    Returns:
        None

    Example:
        ```python
        draw_button(ui_turtle, -100, -250, 80, 30, "lightblue", "Click Me")
        ```
    """
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x, y)
    t.pendown()

    # Draw button background
    t.fillcolor(fill_color)
    t.begin_fill()
    for _ in range(2):
        t.forward(width)
        t.left(90)
        t.forward(height)
        t.left(90)
    t.end_fill()

    # Add text
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x + width/2, y + height/2 - 10)
    t.color(text_color)
    t.write(text, align="center", font=("Arial", 12, "bold"))
    t.color("black")  # Reset color

def draw_square(t, x, y, size, color):
    """
    Draw a square on the canvas using turtle graphics.

    Args:
        t (turtle.Turtle): The turtle object to use for drawing
        x (float): X-coordinate of the bottom-left corner
        y (float): Y-coordinate of the bottom-left corner
        size (float): Width and height of the square in pixels
        color (str): Color name or hex code for filling the square

    Returns:
        None

    Example:
        ```python
        draw_square(my_turtle, 100, 100, 50, "#769656")
        ```
    """
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x, y)
    t.pendown()
    t.fillcolor(color)
    t.begin_fill()
    for _ in range(4):
        t.forward(size)
        t.left(90)
    t.end_fill()

def draw_ui_elements():
    """
    Draw all UI controls and labels for the application.

    This function creates:
    - Theme selector buttons for each available color theme
    - Board size controls (+ and - buttons)
    - Animation toggle button
    - Play Game button

    Returns:
        None

    Note:
        This function uses the global variables `current_size`, `current_theme`,
        and `animation_on` to determine the current state of the UI elements.
    """
    global current_size, current_theme

    ui_drawer.clear()

    # Define y positions
    theme_y = -250
    size_y = -308
    play_y = -384

    # 1. Draw theme selector label and buttons
    ui_drawer.penup()
    ui_drawer.goto(-290, theme_y + 5)
    ui_drawer.write("Themes: ", align="left", font=("Arial", 14, "bold"))

    # Draw theme buttons
    button_width = 70
    button_height = 30
    x_pos = -200

    for theme in color_themes:
        # Use the theme's dark color for the button
        button_color = color_themes[theme]["dark"]

        # Determine proper text color - white for dark backgrounds
        text_color = "white"

        # Draw the button
        draw_button(ui_drawer, x_pos, theme_y, button_width, button_height, 
                   button_color, theme, text_color)

        # Draw border for all buttons (white/transparent for non-selected)
        ui_drawer.penup()
        ui_drawer.goto(x_pos, theme_y)
        ui_drawer.pendown()

        # Black border for active theme, white for others
        if theme == current_theme:
            ui_drawer.pensize(1)
            ui_drawer.color("black")
        else:
            ui_drawer.pensize(1)
            ui_drawer.color("white")

        for _ in range(2):
            ui_drawer.forward(button_width)
            ui_drawer.left(90)
            ui_drawer.forward(button_height)
            ui_drawer.left(90)
        ui_drawer.pensize(1)
        ui_drawer.color("black")  # Reset color for next operations

        x_pos += button_width + 10

    # 2. Draw board size controls and animation toggle on the same row
    ui_drawer.penup()
    ui_drawer.goto(-290, size_y)
    ui_drawer.write("Board Size:", align="left", font=("Arial", 14, "bold"))

    # Draw decrease size button (minus)
    draw_button(ui_drawer, -170, size_y, 40, 25, "lightgray", "−")

    # Draw current size label - vertically centered between buttons
    ui_drawer.penup()
    ui_drawer.goto(-100, size_y)  # Centered between buttons
    ui_drawer.write(f"{current_size}×{current_size}", align="center", font=("Arial", 14, "bold"))

    # Draw increase size button (plus)
    draw_button(ui_drawer, -70, size_y, 40, 25, "lightgray", "+")

    # Draw Animation Toggle button (on same row as size controls)
    ui_drawer.penup()
    ui_drawer.goto(100, size_y)
    ui_drawer.write("Animation:", align="left", font=("Arial", 14, "bold"))

    # Draw the toggle button
    animation_state = "ON" if animation_on else "OFF"
    animation_color = "lightgreen" if animation_on else "lightgray"
    draw_button(ui_drawer, 210, size_y, 60, 25, animation_color, animation_state)

    # 3. Draw Play Game button - centered and larger
    draw_button(ui_drawer, -150, play_y, 300, 50, "green", "Play Game", "white")

    screen.update()

def handle_click(x, y):
    """
    Master click event handler that delegates to specific handlers.

    This function checks all clickable elements on the screen and
    responds accordingly when a click is detected.

    Args:
        x (float): X-coordinate of the click
        y (float): Y-coordinate of the click

    Returns:
        None
    """
    if check_theme_button_click(x, y):
        return

    if check_size_button_click(x, y):
        return

    if check_animation_button_click(x, y):
        return

    if check_play_button_click(x, y):
        return

def main():
    """
    Main application entry point.

    This function initializes the application, draws the chess board and UI elements,
    and sets up the event handlers.

    Returns:
        None

    Example:
        ```python
        if __name__ == "__main__":
            main()
        ```
    """
    global current_size, current_theme

    # Default to 8x8 board size
    current_size = 8

    # Calculate appropriate square size based on screen
    square_size = min(600 // current_size, 70)

    # Draw the chess board
    draw_board(current_size, square_size, current_theme)

    # Draw UI elements
    draw_ui_elements()

    # Set up click handler
    screen.onclick(handle_click)

    # Start the main loop
    screen.mainloop()

def play_game():
    """
    Display a message when the Play Game button is clicked.

    This is a placeholder function that shows a message in the center of the screen
    and waits for a click to return to the board drawer.

    Returns:
        None
    """
    # Clear previous message if any
    board_drawer.clear()
    ui_drawer.clear()

    # Draw a message in the center of the screen
    message_turtle = turtle.Turtle()
    message_turtle.hideturtle()
    message_turtle.penup()
    message_turtle.goto(0, 0)
    message_turtle.color("green")
    message_turtle.write("Welcome to Chess Game!\n\nThis is a placeholder for the actual game.\n\nClick anywhere to return to the board drawer.", 
                       align="center", font=("Arial", 20, "bold"))

    # Wait for click to go back
    def go_back(x, y):
        message_turtle.clear()
        # Redraw the board
        square_size = min(600 // current_size, 70)
        draw_board(current_size, square_size, current_theme)
        draw_ui_elements()
        # Reset the click handler
        screen.onclick(handle_click)

    screen.onclick(go_back)

def toggle_animation():
    """
    Toggle animation effects on or off.

    This function switches the animation state between on and off,
    and updates the UI to reflect the change.

    Returns:
        None

    Note:
        When animation is on, drawing operations are visible.
        When animation is off, drawings appear instantly.
    """
    global animation_on
    animation_on = not animation_on

    # Update the tracer setting
    screen.tracer(1 if animation_on else 0)

    # Redraw UI to update the animation button
    draw_ui_elements()

def draw_square(t, x, y, size, color):
    """
    Draw a square on the canvas using turtle graphics.

    Args:
        t (turtle.Turtle): The turtle object to use for drawing
        x (float): X-coordinate of the bottom-left corner
        y (float): Y-coordinate of the bottom-left corner
        size (float): Width and height of the square in pixels
        color (str): Color name or hex code for filling the square

    Returns:
        None

    Example:
        ```python
        draw_square(my_turtle, 100, 100, 50, "#769656")
        ```
    """
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x, y)
    t.pendown()
    t.fillcolor(color)
    t.begin_fill()
    for _ in range(4):
        t.forward(size)
        t.left(90)
    t.end_fill()

def draw_board(size=8, square_size=50, theme_name="Classic"):
    """
    Draw a complete chess board with the given parameters.

    This function creates a chess board centered on the screen with the specified
    size, square dimensions, and color theme. For standard 8×8 boards, it also
    adds row and column labels (a-h, 1-8).

    Args:
        size (int): Number of squares per side (default: 8)
        square_size (int): Size of each square in pixels (default: 50)
        theme_name (str): Name of the color theme to use (default: "Classic")

    Returns:
        None

    Note:
        The board is drawn centered on the screen, with the origin (0,0) at the center.
        Row and column labels are only added for standard 8×8 boards.
    """
    # Get colors from the theme
    light_color = color_themes[theme_name]["light"]
    dark_color = color_themes[theme_name]["dark"]

    # Calculate the total board size
    board_size = size * square_size

    # Calculate starting position to center the board
    start_x = -board_size / 2
    start_y = -board_size / 2 + 100  # Moved up to reduce top padding

    # Clear previous drawings
    board_drawer.clear()

    # Draw all squares
    for row in range(size):
        for col in range(size):
            # Determine square color (alternating pattern)
            color = light_color if (row + col) % 2 == 0 else dark_color

            # Calculate position for this square
            x = start_x + col * square_size
            y = start_y + row * square_size

            # Draw the square
            draw_square(board_drawer, x, y, square_size, color)

    # Draw border around the board
    board_drawer.penup()
    board_drawer.goto(start_x, start_y)
    board_drawer.pendown()
    board_drawer.pensize(1)  # Reduced border size
    board_drawer.color("black")
    for _ in range(4):
        board_drawer.forward(board_size)
        board_drawer.left(90)

    # Draw labels (a-h, 1-8) for a standard 8x8 board
    if size == 8:
        # Draw column labels (a-h)
        board_drawer.penup()
        for col in range(8):
            x = start_x + col * square_size + square_size / 2
            y = start_y - 25
            board_drawer.goto(x, y)
            board_drawer.write(chr(97 + col), align="center", font=("Arial", 12, "normal"))

        # Draw row labels (1-8)
        for row in range(8):
            x = start_x - 25
            y = start_y + row * square_size + square_size / 2 - 6
            board_drawer.goto(x, y)
            board_drawer.write(str(row + 1), align="center", font=("Arial", 12, "normal"))

    screen.update()  # Update the screen after drawing

def draw_button(t, x, y, width, height, fill_color, text, text_color="black"):
    """
    Draw an interactive button with text.

    Args:
        t (turtle.Turtle): The turtle object to use for drawing
        x (float): X-coordinate of the bottom-left corner
        y (float): Y-coordinate of the bottom-left corner
        width (float): Width of the button in pixels
        height (float): Height of the button in pixels
        fill_color (str): Color name or hex code for the button background
        text (str): Text to display on the button
        text_color (str, optional): Color for the button text (default: "black")

    Returns:
        None

    Example:
        ```python
        draw_button(ui_turtle, -100, -250, 80, 30, "lightblue", "Click Me")
        ```
    """
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x, y)
    t.pendown()

    # Draw button background
    t.fillcolor(fill_color)
    t.begin_fill()
    for _ in range(2):
        t.forward(width)
        t.left(90)
        t.forward(height)
        t.left(90)
    t.end_fill()

    # Add text
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x + width/2, y + height/2 - 10)
    t.color(text_color)
    t.write(text, align="center", font=("Arial", 12, "bold"))
    t.color("black")  # Reset color

def draw_ui_elements():
    """
    Draw all UI controls and labels for the application.

    This function creates:
    - Theme selector buttons for each available color theme
    - Board size controls (+ and - buttons)
    - Animation toggle button
    - Play Game button

    Returns:
        None

    Note:
        This function uses the global variables `current_size`, `current_theme`,
        and `animation_on` to determine the current state of the UI elements.
    """
    global current_size, current_theme

    ui_drawer.clear()

    # Define y positions
    theme_y = -250
    size_y = -308
    play_y = -384

    # 1. Draw theme selector label and buttons
    ui_drawer.penup()
    ui_drawer.goto(-290, theme_y + 5)
    ui_drawer.write("Themes: ", align="left", font=("Arial", 14, "bold"))

    # Draw theme buttons
    button_width = 70
    button_height = 30
    x_pos = -200

    for theme in color_themes:
        # Use the theme's dark color for the button
        button_color = color_themes[theme]["dark"]

        # Determine proper text color - white for dark backgrounds
        text_color = "white"

        # Draw the button
        draw_button(ui_drawer, x_pos, theme_y, button_width, button_height, 
                   button_color, theme, text_color)

        # Draw border for all buttons (white/transparent for non-selected)
        ui_drawer.penup()
        ui_drawer.goto(x_pos, theme_y)
        ui_drawer.pendown()

        # Black border for active theme, white for others
        if theme == current_theme:
            ui_drawer.pensize(1)
            ui_drawer.color("black")
        else:
            ui_drawer.pensize(1)
            ui_drawer.color("white")

        for _ in range(2):
            ui_drawer.forward(button_width)
            ui_drawer.left(90)
            ui_drawer.forward(button_height)
            ui_drawer.left(90)
        ui_drawer.pensize(1)
        ui_drawer.color("black")  # Reset color for next operations

        x_pos += button_width + 10

    # 2. Draw board size controls and animation toggle on the same row
    ui_drawer.penup()
    ui_drawer.goto(-290, size_y)
    ui_drawer.write("Board Size:", align="left", font=("Arial", 14, "bold"))

    # Draw decrease size button (minus)
    draw_button(ui_drawer, -170, size_y, 40, 25, "lightgray", "−")

    # Draw current size label - vertically centered between buttons
    ui_drawer.penup()
    ui_drawer.goto(-100, size_y)  # Centered between buttons
    ui_drawer.write(f"{current_size}×{current_size}", align="center", font=("Arial", 14, "bold"))

    # Draw increase size button (plus)
    draw_button(ui_drawer, -70, size_y, 40, 25, "lightgray", "+")

    # Draw Animation Toggle button (on same row as size controls)
    ui_drawer.penup()
    ui_drawer.goto(100, size_y)
    ui_drawer.write("Animation:", align="left", font=("Arial", 14, "bold"))

    # Draw the toggle button
    animation_state = "ON" if animation_on else "OFF"
    animation_color = "lightgreen" if animation_on else "lightgray"
    draw_button(ui_drawer, 210, size_y, 60, 25, animation_color, animation_state)

    # 3. Draw Play Game button - centered and larger
    draw_button(ui_drawer, -150, play_y, 300, 50, "green", "Play Game", "white")

    screen.update()

def handle_click(x, y):
    """
    Master click event handler that delegates to specific handlers.

    This function checks all clickable elements on the screen and
    responds accordingly when a click is detected.

    Args:
        x (float): X-coordinate of the click
        y (float): Y-coordinate of the click

    if check_theme_button_click(x, y):
        return

    if check_size_button_click(x, y):
        return

    if check_animation_button_click(x, y):
        return

    if check_play_button_click(x, y):

def check_theme_button_click(x, y):
    """
    Check if a theme button was clicked and respond accordingly.

    Args:
        x (float): X-coordinate of the click
        y (float): Y-coordinate of the click

    Returns:
        bool: True if a theme button was clicked, False otherwise

    Note:
        This function will change the current theme if a theme button is clicked.
    """
    theme_y = -250
    button_width = 70
    button_height = 30
    x_pos = -200

    for theme in color_themes:
        # Check if click is within this button
        if x_pos <= x <= x_pos + button_width and theme_y <= y <= theme_y + button_height:
            change_theme(theme)
            return True

        x_pos += button_width + 10

    return False

def check_size_button_click(x, y):
    """
    Check if a size control button was clicked and respond accordingly.

    Args:
        x (float): X-coordinate of the click
        y (float): Y-coordinate of the click

    Returns:
        bool: True if a size control button was clicked, False otherwise

    Note:
        This function will increase or decrease the board size if the
        corresponding button is clicked.
    """
    size_y = -308

    # Check decrease button
    if -170 <= x <= -130 and size_y <= y <= size_y + 25:
        change_board_size(-1)
        return True

    # Check increase button
    if -70 <= x <= -30 and size_y <= y <= size_y + 25:
        change_board_size(1)
        return True

    return False

def change_theme(theme_name):
    """
    Change the color theme and redraw the board.

    Args:
        theme_name (str): Name of the theme to apply (must be a key in color_themes)

    Returns:
        None

    Raises:
        KeyError: If the theme_name is not found in color_themes

    Example:
        ```python
        change_theme("Blue")  # Changes to the blue theme
        ```
    """
    global current_theme
    current_theme = theme_name

    # Calculate appropriate square size based on screen and board size
    square_size = min(600 // current_size, 70)

    # Redraw the board with new theme
    draw_board(current_size, square_size, current_theme)

    # Redraw UI elements
    draw_ui_elements()

def change_board_size(delta):
    """
    Change the board size by the specified delta.

    Args:
        delta (int): Amount to change the board size by (+1 to increase, -1 to decrease)

    Returns:
        None

    Note:
        The board size is constrained to be between 4 and 16 inclusive.
        The square size is automatically adjusted to fit the screen.
    """
    global current_size

    # Update size with constraints
    new_size = current_size + delta
    if 4 <= new_size <= 16:
        current_size = new_size

        # Calculate appropriate square size based on screen
        square_size = min(600 // current_size, 70)

        # Redraw the board
        draw_board(current_size, square_size, current_theme)

        # Redraw UI elements
        draw_ui_elements()

def toggle_animation():
    """
    Toggle animation effects on or off.

    This function switches the animation state between on and off,
    and updates the UI to reflect the change.

    Returns:
        None

    Note:
        When animation is on, drawing operations are visible.
        When animation is off, drawings appear instantly.
    """
    global animation_on
    animation_on = not animation_on

    # Update the tracer setting
    screen.tracer(1 if animation_on else 0)

    # Redraw UI to update the animation button
    draw_ui_elements()

def play_game():
    """
    Display a message when the Play Game button is clicked.

    This is a placeholder function that shows a message in the center of the screen
    and waits for a click to return to the board drawer.

    Returns:
        None
    """
    # Clear previous message if any
    board_drawer.clear()
    ui_drawer.clear()

    # Draw a message in the center of the screen
    message_turtle = turtle.Turtle()
    message_turtle.hideturtle()
    message_turtle.penup()
    message_turtle.goto(0, 0)
    message_turtle.color("green")
    message_turtle.write("Welcome to Chess Game!\n\nThis is a placeholder for the actual game.\n\nClick anywhere to return to the board drawer.", 
                       align="center", font=("Arial", 20, "bold"))

    # Wait for click to go back
    def go_back(x, y):
        message_turtle.clear()
        # Redraw the board
        square_size = min(600 // current_size, 70)
        draw_board(current_size, square_size, current_theme)
        draw_ui_elements()
        # Reset the click handler
        screen.onclick(handle_click)

    screen.onclick(go_back)

def main():
    """
    Main application entry point.

    This function initializes the application, draws the chess board and UI elements,
    and sets up the event handlers.

    Returns:
        None

    Example:
        ```python
        if __name__ == "__main__":
            main()
        ```
    """
    global current_size, current_theme

    # Default to 8x8 board size
    current_size = 8

    # Calculate appropriate square size based on screen
    square_size = min(600 // current_size, 70)

    # Draw the chess board
    draw_board(current_size, square_size, current_theme)

    # Draw UI elements
    draw_ui_elements()

    # Set up click handler
    screen.onclick(handle_click)

    # Start the main loop
    screen.mainloop()

docs.title: Board Size

  • Click the + button to increase the size

The application automatically adjusts the square sizes to fit the screen.

The animation toggle controls how the board is drawn:

  • OFF: The board appears instantly (default)
  • ON: You can see the drawing process animated

docs.title: Chess Game Integration

docs.title: Board Labels
docs.text:
For standard 8×8 boards, the application automatically adds:

  • Column labels (a-h)
  • Row numbers (1-8)

This makes the board suitable for standard chess notation.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The application includes robust error handling:

  • Graceful exit with Ctrl+C
  • Exception reporting
  • Protection against invalid board sizes

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide will help you get started with the Chess Board Drawer application.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Make sure you have Python 3.6 or newer installed
  2. Download the turtle_chessboard.py file
  3. Ensure you have the Tkinter library installed (included with most Python installations)

docs.title: Running the Application
docs.text:
Simply run the Python script:

python turtle_chessboard.py

The application will open in a new window showing a chess board with UI controls at the bottom.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
Once the application is running:

  1. Select a theme by clicking on one of the theme buttons
  2. Adjust board size using the + and - buttons
  3. Toggle animation with the Animation button
  4. Launch a chess game by clicking the "Play Game" button

docs.title: Understanding the Interface
docs.text:
1. Chess Board: The main visualization area showing the current board
  2. Theme Selection: Buttons to change the board's color scheme
  3. Size Controls: Buttons to increase or decrease the board dimensions
  4. Animation Toggle: Button to turn animation effects on or off
  5. Play Button: Launch the associated chess game

A vibrant red theme for a bold, striking appearance.

  • Light squares: #F5D5D5 (light pink)
  • Dark squares: #D35D6E (raspberry red)

docs.title: Selecting a Theme
docs.text:
To change the theme of your chess board:

  1. Locate the Themes section in the UI (at the bottom of the application)
  2. Click on any of the theme buttons to apply it
  3. The board will update immediately with the new colors

docs.title: Adding Custom Themes
docs.text:
If you're a developer, you can easily add your own custom themes to the application by modifying the color_themes dictionary in the source code:

# Add your custom theme
color_themes["MyTheme"] = {"light": "#YOURCOLOR1", "dark": "#YOURCOLOR2"}

When choosing colors for a custom theme, consider these guidelines:

  • Ensure high contrast between light and dark squares
  • Test your theme for visibility of chess pieces (especially in the chess game component)
  • Use web-safe colors or hexadecimal color codes

docs.title: Theme Implementation Details
docs.text:
Each theme in the application is implemented as a dictionary entry with two color values:

color_themes = {
    "Classic": {"light": "#EEEED2", "dark": "#769656"},
    # Other themes...
}

When a theme is selected, the application:

  1. Retrieves the light and dark colors from the theme dictionary
  2. Redraws the entire board using the new colors
  3. Updates the UI to highlight the currently selected theme

For more details on the implementation, see the change_theme() function in the API reference.
